title: skills for driving buses, taxis, limousines and ride-hailing vehicles
objectives: Define the various types of Class 2 and Class 4 vehicles and describe their uses
Describe how to safely deal with common driving situations such as leaving the curb and passing parked cars
Identify and describe key regulations that apply to operating buses, taxis, limousines and ride-hailing vehicles
List and describe the requirements for operating a school bus
Describe the special considerations and regulations for driving an emergency vehicle

sections.title: Passenger safety and manoeuvring
points: Passenger safety is always more important than meeting schedules.
Most bus passenger injuries come from stopping, starting or turning too quickly, or opening/closing doors too fast.
Keep a safe following distance and avoid getting blocked in so you always have an escape route.
Before leaving the curb, check your side mirror and over your shoulder — never rely on mirrors alone.
Watch that the rear of the bus doesn't swing over the sidewalk and hit pedestrians, cyclists, poles or sign posts.
When passing parked cars, watch for vehicles pulling out, doors opening and pedestrians stepping out between cars.
Clues to hazards: front wheels turned out, driver behind the wheel, exhaust, brake or back-up lights, people near the road.
mustKnow: A bus seats more than 10 persons including the driver; a taxi or limousine carries not more than 10.
A large capacity limousine carries more than 10 and up to 24 persons, including the driver.
Public transit buses have right-of-way when signalling to leave a bus stop or curb lane where the speed limit is less than 60 km/h and the bus displays a yield sign.
The right-of-way rule doesn't remove responsibility — the bus driver must still ensure it's safe before moving into traffic.

check.q: The transit bus right-of-way rule applies in areas where the speed limit is:
check.explanation: The Motor Vehicle Act gives transit buses right-of-way leaving a stop where the speed limit is less than 60 km/h.

check.q: Before leaving the curb, in addition to your side mirror you should check:
check.explanation: Don't rely on side mirrors alone — look over your shoulder to confirm traffic is clear before leaving the curb.

sections.title: Operating a bus, taxi, limousine or ride-hailing vehicle
points: You need a passenger transportation licence to be responsible for a vehicle transporting passengers for hire.
When stopping on a highway, signal, be visible from at least 85 metres front and behind, and leave 3 metres for passing traffic.
Never collect fares, make change, or take on or let off passengers while the vehicle is moving.
Passengers may not stand unless the vehicle's passenger transportation licence allows it; the standing capacity must be displayed.
You may refuse a passenger who smokes, uses profane language or acts in a disorderly or offensive manner, or when full.
You can't refuse someone because of a disability, and service animals such as guide dogs must be allowed with their owners.
Some municipalities require taxi and limousine drivers to hold a chauffeur's permit, usually issued by the municipal police.
mustKnow: Stop where drivers can see your vehicle from at least 85 metres (285 ft) in front and behind, leaving at least three metres (10 ft) on the left.
Up to two passengers may sit to your right in a sedan-type vehicle, only with designated seating positions and seatbelts.
It's illegal to smoke in any motor vehicle when there are passengers under 16 years old.
If you order a person out, ensure they can disembark safely where they can reasonably find alternate transportation.
Vehicles seating more than 12 occupants including the driver must have aisle lights kept on between sunset and sunrise.

check.q: How many passengers may sit to the driver's right in a sedan-type vehicle?
check.explanation: Up to two passengers may sit on your right if there is room to operate safely and designated seatbelt-equipped positions.

check.q: When taking on passengers on a highway, other drivers must be able to see your vehicle from at least:
check.explanation: Stop where your vehicle is visible from at least 85 metres (285 ft) in front and behind.

sections.title: Vehicle condition, equipment and baggage
points: A B.C.-licensed vehicle with a passenger transportation plate must display a valid inspection decal and carry the certificate.
Your bus or taxi must be clean and sanitary at all times.
End the trip if a problem could endanger passenger safety or comfort; fix it before continuing.
After a crash or breakdown, arrange onward transport for your passengers with as little delay as possible.
When fuelling: engine off, no radio transmitting, no open flame, and keep the nozzle in contact with the filler pipe.
Load baggage so it can't fall on passengers, doesn't block boarding, and never blocks any aisle or exit.
Don't smoke with passengers in your vehicle, moving or not, and never be under the influence of alcohol on duty.
mustKnow: Commercial passenger vehicles seating more than 10 occupants including the driver must carry a first-aid kit, a spare tire and at least one fire extinguisher.
The carrier is responsible for ensuring emergency equipment is available and in working order.
Vehicles seating more than 12 including the driver need an emergency exit door or emergency windows.
Vehicles seating more than 10 passengers must carry warning devices such as flags and flares.
Report any defect or deficiency in writing to your carrier when you find it or by the end of that day.

check.q: A defect that could make your vehicle unsafe must be reported to the carrier:
choices: In writing by the end of that day
check.explanation: Defect reports must be made in writing and given to the carrier when found or by the end of that day.

check.q: Who is responsible for ensuring the emergency equipment is available and in working order?
check.explanation: The carrier is responsible for ensuring the required emergency equipment is available and working.

sections.title: Operating a school bus
points: Test school bus brakes every day and never operate the bus unless the brakes are safe.
Never transport passengers on a defective school bus; an unfit bus can't operate until defects are fixed.
Ensure all passengers are off and the engine is turned off before refuelling.
Passengers may not stand — everyone must be seated before you move the bus.
Before opening doors: full stop, 3 metres of road on the left, visible from 60 metres either direction, right side only.
Use alternating flashing red lights whenever passengers cross the road; all drivers must stop for them.
Turn off flashing lights and draw in the stop sign once passengers are safely aboard or across the road.
mustKnow: School buses must display two 'School Bus' signs, front and rear, with black letters at least 20 cm high on a yellow background.
The school bus floor must be washed with a disinfectant solution at least once a week.
Passengers must enter or leave a school bus from the right side only.
Other drivers must be able to see your stopped school bus from at least 60 metres in either direction.
A rental replacement bus must comply with school bus regulations, and you must notify Commercial Vehicle Safety and Enforcement as soon as possible.

check.q: How often must you test the brakes on a school bus?
check.explanation: School bus brakes must be tested every day, and the bus must not operate unless the brakes are safe.

check.q: The letters on a school bus sign must be black on a yellow background and at least:
check.explanation: 'School Bus' signs at the front and rear must have black letters at least 20 cm high on a yellow background.

sections.title: Operating emergency vehicles
points: Ambulance flashing red lights may be used only when responding to an emergency call or transporting a patient.
You may exceed speed limits and pass red lights or stop signs only if you give other drivers appropriate warning.
Use both flashing red lights and the siren to warn other drivers.
Use caution at all times — other drivers may not see or hear your warning.
mustKnow: Before exceeding limits or driving through stop signals, consider: the condition and use of the highway, the amount of traffic, and the seriousness of the emergency.

check.q: When may an ambulance driver use flashing red lights?
choices: Only when responding to an emergency call or transporting a patient
Any time the ambulance is on duty
check.explanation: Flashing red lights are used only when responding to an emergency call or transporting a patient.

summary: Passenger safety always comes before schedules — drive smoothly and check passengers are settled before moving.
Know the key distances: visible from 85 m when stopping on a highway (60 m for school buses) and leave 3 m on the left.
Carry the required emergency equipment, report defects in writing by the end of the day, and never continue with an unsafe vehicle.
School buses need daily brake tests, two 20 cm 'School Bus' signs, seated passengers, and right-side boarding only.
Emergency vehicles may exceed limits only with lights and siren, weighing highway conditions, traffic and the seriousness of the emergency.
